# Upstream reference

The Go port is measured against the Python `shepherd` monorepo. This file
records the pinned version the vectors and golden files in this directory
were produced from — the §13 v1.0-readiness "upstream shepherd2 version
recorded" item.

- **Repository**: https://github.com/shepherd-agents/shepherd
- **Pinned commit**: `d34d5ca334871dfcb5a3dc76dd78045829fa4e56`
- **Components**: `shepherd2` (the ring-0/ring-1 reference kernel),
  `shepherd-workspace` 0.3.1 / `shepherd2` 0.1.0a0 per the repo's
  pyproject at the pin
- **Interpreter recorded at generation time**: CPython 3.13.13

## What the pin is used for

- `kernel_abi_v0.json` is the frozen ABI golden, copied verbatim from the
  reference at the pin. The CI `golden drift (vs pinned Python reference)`
  job clones the repository at this commit and compares hashes, so the
  golden cannot drift from upstream silently.
- `canonical_*`, `store_vectors_v0.json`, `execution_vectors_v0.json`,
  and `materialize_vectors_v0.json` were generated by the Python scripts
  in this directory (`generate_*.py`), each run against the pin. Their
  content hashes are pinned in `golden_provenance_test.go`, which also
  records `generatedBy` per file.

## Re-pinning

Upstream is expected to move; this port is deliberately frozen against the
pin above. When the pin is updated on purpose:

1. Regenerate every vector file with the `generate_*.py` scripts against
   the new commit (same interpreter assumptions; record it here).
2. Update the pinned content hashes in `golden_provenance_test.go` in the
   same commit.
3. Update the pinned commit in the CI golden-drift job
   (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) and in this file together.
